specification.objective: Implement issue #76 so employee responses report linked account presence and access role, the admin editor represents account roles without confusing them with job titles, and role changes remain explicit and atomic.

requirements.statement: Employee list, detail, create, and update responses expose hasAccount and accessRole from the linked UserAccount employee_id relation; no account yields hasAccount=false and accessRole=null.
Employee.role remains the descriptive job title. accessRole is account authorization and linked manager/employee roles are represented accurately; admin is represented but not editable.
Employees without a linked account are distinguished and cannot be assigned an access role through the employee editor; unknown legacy account state is read-only.
Existing update payloads that omit accessRole remain accepted and preserve the linked account role. Older employee responses missing account metadata remain parseable as unknown state.
Unsupported request roles, explicit role changes without an account, and attempts to change an admin role are rejected without persisting employee or account mutations.
The response exposes only account link presence and role; no account identifiers, email, or authentication data are added.

acceptance_criteria.statement: List/detail/create/update responses report hasAccount=true and the actual employee/manager account role; no linked account reports false and null, while all existing response fields remain present.
Editing an employee with a manager account displays manager, keeps Employee.role as the job title, and an unchanged access role is omitted from the request so the existing role is preserved.
An employee without an account sees a no-access state and no access-role control; a linked admin sees an explicit non-editable admin state.
A response payload from the old contract still parses with account state unknown, and old update payloads without accessRole are accepted.
An invalid accessRole request, a valid role change for an unlinked employee, and a role change for an admin account do not persist changes to employee fields, account roles, or success audit records.

invariants.statement: Employee.role continues to store and return the employee's descriptive job title; account role is never inferred from or written into it.
Only employee and manager are request-selectable roles. Admin remains visible and read-only, and account creation/linking and authorization policy do not change.
Omitting accessRole from an update does not alter the linked account role.

forbidden_states.statement: The employee editor defaults an unknown or missing account role to employee or permits access-role changes when there is no linked account.
A rejected role update leaves dirty employee fields, account data, or success audit writes in the database session.
Account identifiers, email, password, or authentication details are added to employee responses.

inputs.statement: Employee.account and UserAccount.employee_id relation, current EmployeeProfileResponse, and EmployeeDraftPayload.
Issue #76 acceptance criteria and the focused Odesa contract review.

outputs.statement: Backward-compatible employee response metadata and a form that only offers valid explicit role edits.
Regression evidence for response serialization, UI states, role preservation, and rejected role mutations.

failure_semantics.statement: Invalid roles fail request validation before service mutation; missing-account and admin role changes are rejected before employee/account fields are assigned.
If the new account fields are absent in a legacy response, the parser keeps account state unknown and the editor does not offer role mutation.
